claims.text: A physics-informed machine-learning framework integrating experimental data, elemental descriptors, and thermo-kinetic parameters can rapidly identify RHEA compositions optimized for strength, ductility, and low density.
Traditional RHEA development relies on simulation-heavy thermo-kinetic and experimental approaches.
Active learning can efficiently screen and refine RHEA candidates within a vast multi-principal-element composition space.
RHEAs are relevant to elevated-temperature service conditions.
The candidate alloys are evaluated under high-stress conditions typical of refractory materials.
RHEAs occupy a multi-principal-element composition space comprising mostly refractory elements.
Integrating elemental descriptors with thermo-kinetic parameters can mediate optimal phase formation and microstructural features.
Atomic-size differences in HEAs can displace atoms from ideal lattice sites and produce local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions and dislocation impediments can balance strength, ductility, and density in the proposed RHEAs.
The framework learns nonlinear relationships between composition and mechanical properties from experimental data and physicochemical descriptors.
A strength-ductility trade-off is a long-standing challenge in refractory and other high-performance alloy design.
The machine-learning framework can predict RHEAs that overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
The machine-learning framework can reduce alloy density while maintaining improved mechanical properties.
Machine-learning-predicted RHEAs will have significantly greater intrinsic strength and ductility at lower density than conventionally designed alloys.
The proposed framework will substantially reduce alloy-design time.
Conventional design approaches require extensive thermo-kinetic simulations and labor-intensive experiments.
The effectiveness of the framework depends on the availability and quality of experimental data and descriptors.
Predictions in sparsely characterized composition regions are less certain.
The magnitude of property improvement and predictive accuracy in uncharted composition regions remain uncertain.
